title: Array Memory Layout
concept: An array is an apartment tightly spaced in memory.

steps.title: Include stdio.h header
steps.explanation:
Standard input/output header for using `printf`.

In this lesson, the address output confirms that array elements are placed contiguously in memory.

steps.title: Start main function
steps.explanation:
The main stack frame is created and the array `arr` is placed within it.

An array allocates contiguous space equal to “number of elements x type size” at a time.

steps.title: Array declaration and memory allocation
steps.explanation:
`int arr[3] = {10, 20, 30};` stores 3 ints in contiguous memory.

The key is that the spacing between elements is constant at `sizeof(int)`, and this rule is the basis for pointer arithmetic.

steps.title: address of first element
steps.explanation:
`&arr[0]` prints the array start address.

The array name `arr` behaves like `&arr[0]` in many expressions, from which the addresses of the remaining elements can be computed.

steps.title: address of second element
steps.explanation:
`&arr[1]` is an address that is `sizeof(int)` larger than `&arr[0]`.

That is, the rule `&arr[n] = &arr[0] + n * sizeof(int)` holds true.

steps.title: address of third element
steps.explanation:
`&arr[2]` is also a consecutive address evaluated by the same rules.

Because arrays are contiguous storage structures, out-of-range index access is very dangerous.
steps.stdout:
arr[0] Address: 0x1000
arr[1] Address: 0x1004
arr[2] Address: 0x1008

steps.title: Program exit
steps.explanation:
It terminates with `return 0;` and the array memory on the stack is also cleaned up.

Key point: Array elements are placed contiguously and the address spacing is as large as the type.

quiz.question: double arr[2]; If &arr[0] is address 100, what about &arr[1]?
quiz.explanation:
A `double` is usually 8 bytes.
Since the array is tightly contiguous, the next element is located at address 100 + 8 = 108.

misconceptions.wrong: You can change the array size later
misconceptions.correct: The default array in C language is **Fixed Size**.
misconceptions.why:
This is because the moment it is declared, it only takes up that much space on the stack.
To increase you need to use `malloc` and `realloc`.

keyTakeaway: The arrangement is close together. The address difference is as large as the type size (sizeof).
